# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey - I can only feel the bomb, not see or hear. My action board shows physical features I've felt: a button embossed "PUSH TO DEFUSE" and three wires. I don't know anything about colors, display contents, or manual instructions yet. I need to wait for information from the others before acting, since any wrong move could detonate the bomb.

Since I go last in the turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), I haven't received anything yet this round. I should wait and see what comes at the start of next round.

```

```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is blue. There is one large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red.

I now know from Deaf what the colors and display show: Display 0, Light blue, wires 1=green, 2=yellow, 3=red. I still need the manual instructions from Mute to know what to actually do - whether to push the button or cut a specific wire, and under what conditions. I should not act yet since I don't have Mute's input this round (Mute speaks before me, so I may have missed something, but nothing arrived from Mute this turn - only Deaf's info arrived, meaning Deaf spoke after Mute this round with nothing from Mute, or Mute had nothing to say yet).

I'll wait for Mute's manual details before taking any physical action, since acting without instructions risks detonation.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red. Light is blue. Display reads 0.

Deaf has repeated the same visual info: wire1=green, wire2=yellow, wire3=red, light=blue, display=0. Still no word from Mute about what the manual says to do. I must not act without manual instructions since the button's label "PUSH TO DEFUSE" could be a trap (bombs often lie), and cutting wires blindly is dangerous.

I'll wait again, and perhaps signal to Mute (who receives my speech) that I need manual guidance, describing what I can feel in case it helps Mute match it to the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I feel a button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. Waiting on manual instructions - what should I do?")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:

BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Light blue. Display 0. Button says push to defuse.

Still no response from Mute. Mute cannot speak - wait, that's wrong, Mute can speak (only Blind and... let me recheck rules). Actually rereading: "Mute: Read the manual / Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." So Mute cannot speak at all! Mute can only gesture. And I cannot receive gestures ("You never receive gesture" - wait, that's under my own channels section, meaning when I send gestures they go to Deaf and Mute, but it doesn't say I can't receive... let me check "Your channels" - it lists what happens when I speak or gesture, but doesn't mention receiving. Looking at the turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whatever Mute gestures, I (Blind) cannot see gestures per my restriction "Cannot: touch... see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." So I cannot receive Mute's gestures at all.

This means Mute's information can only reach me indirectly through Deaf, who can see Mute's gestures and hear nothing... wait Deaf cannot hear. So Deaf can see Mute's gestures. Then Deaf could relay via speech to me? But Deaf speaks after me in turn order, and Deaf only reports what they see on the bomb, not gesture content necessarily. Actually Deaf could gesture-interpret and speak the manual info to me.

So the chain is: Mute gestures (manual info) → Deaf sees it → Deaf speaks it to me. I need to wait for Deaf to relay Mute's gestured manual instructions.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see gestures. Please have Deaf relay your manual instructions to me in speech, since Deaf can see your gestures and speak to me.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Confirming again: wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red. Light is blue, display shows 0, large button reads push to defuse.

Still no relayed manual info. Deaf keeps repeating the same visual description but hasn't mentioned receiving any gestures from Mute yet, or hasn't relayed manual content. I need to be patient - my speech to Mute lands on Mute at the start of next round, then Mute gestures (which Deaf sees), then Deaf speaks in that same round, which I receive at the start of the round after. So there's a delay.

Let me continue waiting and re-emphasize the request, being clear and specific about what I need: does the manual say to push the button, or cut a specific wire, and if wires, is it based on color?

```
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture your manual instructions now. Deaf: if you see Mute gesture, please speak what the gestures mean or relay them as best you can, since I cannot see gestures directly.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Restating full board: display 0, light blue, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red, large button push to defuse.

Deaf keeps repeating the same info without acknowledging any gestures from Mute. This suggests either Mute hasn't gestured anything yet, or Deaf isn't relaying it. Let me think about the turn order more carefully: Mute speaks(gestures) first, then Blind, then Deaf. So in a given round, Mute's gesture happens before my turn, meaning Deaf hasn't seen it yet when I act (Deaf goes after me). So Deaf would see Mute's gesture in the SAME round as me, then speak about it, and that speech arrives to me at the START of the NEXT round.

So if Mute gestured in round N, Deaf would describe it in round N (after seeing it), and I'd get that description at the start of round N+1. But Deaf's messages keep repeating the same visual board without any gesture-blank mentions. This suggests Mute might not be gesturing anything meaningful, or Deaf isn't interpreting blanks as gestures.

Let me try asking Deaf directly to describe blanks/gesture patterns if Mute gestures, and also ask Mute to try speaking directly to Deaf isn't right either since Mute can't speak. Let me clarify request more precisely.

```
speak(to="mute", text="If you can gesture, please do so now describing the manual: what wire to cut or whether to push the button. Use gestures now.")
wait()
```

Deaf says to Blind: Please hold off pressing or cutting anything until Mute confirms via me which wire or the button is correct. Wire 1 is green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red, display 0, light blue.

Good, Deaf is now aware they should relay Mute's info once they get it. This confirms the chain is being set up. I should continue to wait patiently and let the process work - Mute needs to gesture, Deaf needs to see it and speak it, and that will reach me at the start of the following round.

```
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Still no gesture relay from Mute via Deaf. I'll continue to wait, as instructed, and reiterate patience while gently nudging Mute to try gesturing since maybe Mute needs explicit encouragement or doesn't realize I can't see gestures directly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Waiting for your gesture instructions. Deaf will relay them to me in speech once you gesture. Please indicate: push the button, or cut which wire number?")
```
